wholeObject.question: Which micronutrient deserves additional attention when initiating nutrition in a patient at high refeeding risk?
choices: Thiamine
Fluoride only
Vitamin K only
Manganese only
wholeObject.rationale: Thiamine supports carbohydrate metabolism, and renewed calorie delivery can expose deficiency. ASPEN recommends preventive thiamine before feeding or dextrose-containing IV fluids in adults at refeeding risk; vitamin K, manganese or fluoride alone cannot replace it.

individualChoices.text: Thiamine
individualChoices.review: Correct: thiamine prophylaxis precedes feeding or IV dextrose in at-risk adults under the named ASPEN consensus.

individualChoices.text: Fluoride only
individualChoices.review: Incorrect: fluoride alone does not provide the indicated thiamine prophylaxis.

individualChoices.text: Vitamin K only
individualChoices.review: Incorrect: vitamin K alone does not replace thiamine.

individualChoices.text: Manganese only
individualChoices.review: Incorrect: manganese alone does not replace thiamine.

priorReviewFields.proof: Renewed carbohydrate metabolism increases thiamine demand. Vitamin K, manganese and fluoride alone do not provide thiamine; preventive thiamine precedes feeding/dextrose.

wholeObject.question: Which laboratory values require especially close follow-up during refeeding risk?
choices: Phosphate, potassium, magnesium, and glucose
LDL and HDL only
Amylase only
Troponin only
wholeObject.rationale: Refeeding can rapidly lower phosphate, potassium and magnesium while glucose exposure changes. Insulin promotes intracellular potassium and phosphate movement; the magnesium mechanism is less clearly established. Normal initial serum levels do not exclude depleted body stores.

individualChoices.text: Phosphate, potassium, magnesium, and glucose
individualChoices.review: Correct: potassium, phosphate, magnesium and glucose require monitoring during nutrition initiation.

individualChoices.text: LDL and HDL only
individualChoices.review: Incorrect: LDL and HDL alone do not assess the specified electrolyte and glucose changes.

individualChoices.text: Amylase only
individualChoices.review: Incorrect: amylase alone does not replace the electrolyte and glucose monitoring.

individualChoices.text: Troponin only
individualChoices.review: Incorrect: troponin alone does not replace the electrolyte and glucose monitoring.

priorReviewFields.proof: All three electrolytes require follow-up; glucose exposure matters. Insulin-mediated potassium/phosphate movement is distinguished from the less-elucidated magnesium mechanism. LDL/HDL, amylase or troponin alone are inadequate.

wholeObject.question: For an adult at refeeding risk, when does ASPEN recommend the preventive 100 mg thiamine dose?
choices: Only after glucose intolerance develops
Only after the first week of full PN
After the first dextrose bag has finished
Before feeding or dextrose-containing IV fluids
wholeObject.rationale: ASPEN recommends 100 mg thiamine before feeding or before starting dextrose-containing IV fluids in at-risk adults, followed by daily supplementation as indicated. This preventive step does not replace treatment of a suspected deficiency syndrome.

individualChoices.text: Only after glucose intolerance develops
individualChoices.review: Incorrect: prophylaxis should not wait for glucose intolerance.

individualChoices.text: Only after the first week of full PN
individualChoices.review: Incorrect: a week of full PN is too late for the specified preventive step.

individualChoices.text: After the first dextrose bag has finished
individualChoices.review: Incorrect: waiting until the first dextrose bag ends misses the recommended timing.

individualChoices.text: Before feeding or dextrose-containing IV fluids
individualChoices.review: Correct: the preventive 100 mg thiamine dose is before feeding or dextrose-containing IV fluids; prevention does not replace deficiency treatment.

wholeObject.question: An adult at high refeeding risk has severely low phosphate before enteral feeding is started. Which plan best follows the 2020 ASPEN consensus?
choices: Correct the severe deficiency and delay starting or increasing calories until corrected
Start the full energy target while waiting for the next scheduled phosphate result
Advance to full energy as long as baseline potassium is normal
Ignore the phosphate result because the calories will enter through the gut
wholeObject.rationale: Severely low phosphate, potassium, or magnesium calls for delaying calorie initiation or increases until corrected under the 2020 ASPEN consensus. Enteral calories can trigger refeeding physiology, and a normal potassium result does not resolve a severe phosphate deficit. Use cautious advancement and close monitoring rather than starting at the full target.

individualChoices.text: Correct the severe deficiency and delay starting or increasing calories until corrected
individualChoices.review: Correct: the specified severe phosphate deficit warrants correcting it and delaying calorie initiation or escalation under the named adult ASPEN consensus.

individualChoices.text: Start the full energy target while waiting for the next scheduled phosphate result
individualChoices.review: Incorrect: full energy before the severe deficit is corrected defeats the specified prevention step.

individualChoices.text: Advance to full energy as long as baseline potassium is normal
individualChoices.review: Incorrect: normal potassium does not resolve a severe phosphate deficit.

individualChoices.text: Ignore the phosphate result because the calories will enter through the gut
individualChoices.review: Incorrect: enteral calories can produce refeeding physiology.

choicesReviewed.text: Correct the severe deficiency and delay starting or increasing calories until corrected
choicesReviewed.review: Severely low phosphate is explicit: delay calorie initiation/increase until corrected.

choicesReviewed.text: Start the full energy target while waiting for the next scheduled phosphate result
choicesReviewed.review: Full energy while awaiting labs conflicts with severe-deficit recommendation.

choicesReviewed.text: Advance to full energy as long as baseline potassium is normal
choicesReviewed.review: Normal potassium does not resolve phosphate depletion.

choicesReviewed.text: Ignore the phosphate result because the calories will enter through the gut
choicesReviewed.review: Enteral calories can trigger refeeding; route does not exclude the risk.

wholeObject.question: A patient on a dense formula becomes hypernatremic with rising BUN and low urine output. What is the best next action?
choices: Recalculate all water sources, losses, kidney function, and flush delivery
Double the water flush volume immediately without assessing kidney function or the total intake
Reduce the formula protein immediately because rising BUN proves excess protein delivery
Change to a lower-calorie formula while leaving the water budget and delivery record unreviewed
wholeObject.rationale: Inadequate fluid intake can cause hypernatremia, and dehydration may accompany rising BUN and reduced urine output. Kidney dysfunction can also raise BUN, so the findings do not prove that formula density is the sole cause. Promptly reassess hydration, all delivered fluids, losses, and renal status before choosing a patient-specific correction.

individualChoices.text: Recalculate all water sources, losses, kidney function, and flush delivery
individualChoices.review: Correct: reassess delivered water, losses, kidney function and whether flushes were actually given.

individualChoices.text: Double the water flush volume immediately without assessing kidney function or the total intake
individualChoices.review: Incorrect: doubling flushes automatically ignores the complete water budget and patient context.

individualChoices.text: Reduce the formula protein immediately because rising BUN proves excess protein delivery
individualChoices.review: Incorrect: BUN alone does not establish excessive protein intake or a safe protein reduction.

individualChoices.text: Change to a lower-calorie formula while leaving the water budget and delivery record unreviewed
individualChoices.review: Incorrect: changing formula without reviewing total water delivery fails to assess the specified problem.

priorReviewFields.review: Hypernatremia with low intake; dehydration can accompany decreased urine output and elevated BUN, while renal dysfunction can elevate BUN too. Prompt clinical reassessment is a safety inference from these findings and fluid-accumulation warning. No sole-cause diagnosis, protein adjustment, sodium-correction rate or fixed extra water inferred. Full prompt, all four choices, answer key, rationale and stable remediation anchor individually reviewed and rendered.

changedQuestions.question: Why should safe oral intake be reassessed before placing a feeding tube?
choices: Enteral tube feeding should not replace an oral diet that safely meets needs
Tube placement is indicated whenever an oral nutrition supplement is used
Tube feeding prevents aspiration regardless of swallowing function
Tube placement resolves drug-nutrient interactions without medication review
changedQuestions.rationale: Tube feeding supports patients who cannot meet their needs by voluntary oral intake. If safe oral intake already meets those needs, a feeding tube is not indicated solely to deliver nutrition. A tube does not eliminate aspiration risk or medication interactions.

changedQuestions.question: Which outcome is a recognized advantage of enteral nutrition?
choices: Preservation of gastrointestinal structure and function
Avoidance of intestinal absorption because nutrients enter the bloodstream directly
Prevention of aspiration because the feeding tube replaces airway protection
Provision of the full water requirement whenever the calorie target is met
changedQuestions.rationale: Enteral nutrition uses the gut and helps prevent intestinal atrophy. Parenteral nutrition bypasses the gut. Enteral feeding still carries aspiration risk, and meeting calorie needs does not establish adequate water delivery.

changedQuestions.question: What is the most defensible reason to initiate enteral nutrition in a malnourished patient?
choices: Oral intake is inadequate and the gastrointestinal tract is functional
Adequate safe oral intake is present, but a tube formula is more convenient
A central venous line is available, even though safe oral intake meets needs
One low albumin result is present, even though safe oral intake meets needs
changedQuestions.rationale: Enteral support is favored when voluntary oral intake cannot meet nutritional needs and the gut is usable. Formula convenience, an existing intravenous line, or an isolated laboratory result does not override the stated ability to meet needs safely by mouth.

changedQuestions.question: Which route is most appropriate when long-term gastric feeding is expected and gastric function is stable?
choices: A gastrostomy after individualized procedural assessment
A jejunostomy solely because a longer course automatically requires a jejunal destination
Central parenteral nutrition solely because the expected feeding duration is long
A short-term nasal route without reconsidering access as long-term support is planned
changedQuestions.rationale: A gastrostomy provides access through the skin to the stomach, whereas a jejunostomy ends in the small intestine. Nasogastric tubes are primarily short-term access. For the stated long-term gastric plan, consider gastrostomy after individualized assessment; duration alone does not establish a need to bypass a usable stomach.

changedQuestions.question: Which statement about tube selection is most accurate?
choices: Expected duration, anatomy, aspiration risk, gastric function, and medication needs all matter
Expected duration alone determines whether the tube must end in the jejunum
Gastric and jejunal tube tips are interchangeable once the same formula is selected
Choosing a suitable feeding formula removes the need to review medication compatibility
changedQuestions.rationale: Assess both the intended duration and the actual feeding destination. Nasogastric access is primarily short term; gastrostomy and jejunostomy reach different organs. Aspiration remains a risk, and medications require product-specific compatibility and absorption review.

changedQuestions.question: Which additional information is needed to calculate daily formula volume from an order that states only feed at 65 mL per hour?
choices: The daily duration or volume target
The formula calorie density without a feeding duration
The water percentage on the formula label without a feeding duration
The formula bag capacity without a scheduled volume or feeding duration
changedQuestions.rationale: Daily volume equals rate multiplied by the hours actually delivered. Formula energy density, water percentage, or bag capacity alone does not supply the missing daily duration or volume target.

changedQuestions.question: Why should actual delivered volume be audited?
choices: Interruptions can make prescribed and received nutrition substantially different
A correctly programmed hourly rate is sufficient to establish the daily intake
The formula container label establishes intake even when part is not delivered
Ordered calories can substitute for checking how much formula reached the patient
changedQuestions.rationale: Use the amount actually received, not just the order or nominal container amount. If feeding is interrupted or part of a serving is spilled, those portions are not delivered nutrition. The displayed rate must be interpreted with actual feeding time and volume.

changedQuestions.question: What determines total daily water delivery?
choices: Formula free water plus water delivered in flushes, medication fluids, oral intake, and intravenous sources
The full formula volume plus its free-water volume as a second contribution
Formula free water and scheduled flushes, excluding medication and intravenous fluids
The prescribed daily water target regardless of what was actually delivered
changedQuestions.rationale: Add the water delivered from each source once, using formula water content rather than treating all formula volume as water. Medication fluids, including intravenous sources, contribute to the overall intake. Compare actual delivery with the individualized target; a written target is not evidence that the water was received.

changedQuestions.question: Why should ordered and delivered volumes both be charted?
choices: A patient can receive substantially less nutrition than prescribed
The ordered daily volume can be charted as delivered whenever the pump rate is correct
The full bag volume can be charted as intake even if the patient receives only part
The order can replace the intake record once the correct formula has been selected
changedQuestions.rationale: Separate the intended daily volume from the volume actually received. Rate, container size, and formula selection do not prove delivery. Comparing the two records reveals a deficit that would be hidden if ordered volume were copied into the intake record.

changedQuestions.question: A patient on a dense formula becomes hypernatremic with rising BUN and low urine output. What is the best next action?
choices: Recalculate all water sources, losses, kidney function, and flush delivery
Double the water flush volume immediately without assessing kidney function or the total intake
Reduce the formula protein immediately because rising BUN proves excess protein delivery
Change to a lower-calorie formula while leaving the water budget and delivery record unreviewed
changedQuestions.rationale: Inadequate fluid intake can cause hypernatremia, and dehydration may accompany rising BUN and reduced urine output. Kidney dysfunction can also raise BUN, so the findings do not prove that formula density is the sole cause. Promptly reassess hydration, all delivered fluids, losses, and renal status before choosing a patient-specific correction.

changedQuestions.question: A feeding pump shows the prescribed rate, but only 55 percent of the daily target has been delivered for three days. What is the best next action?
choices: Audit interruptions and redesign the safe delivery schedule
Document the full daily target because the displayed hourly rate matches the order
Increase the rate enough to replace the deficit without assessing tolerance or access
Change the formula concentration without checking why the prescribed volume was not delivered
changedQuestions.rationale: The amount actually delivered determines nutrition received; a correct displayed rate does not prove that the scheduled volume reached the patient. Review feeding time, interruptions, and the delivery record, then choose a safe revised plan. Do not compensate automatically without considering the clinical feeding plan.

changedQuestions.question: A home patient uses a 2 kcal per mL formula and receives no scheduled water beyond medication flushes. Which interpretation or management plan is most defensible?
choices: Calculate actual water from the formula and all other sources, then determine supplemental water against an individualized target
Treat the entire formula volume as water and ignore the product water content
Calculate supplemental water from formula water alone without counting medication flushes
Assume that meeting the calorie target establishes adequate daily water delivery
changedQuestions.rationale: The 2 kcal per mL value describes energy density, not the formula water content or the patient's water requirement. Use product water data and the amount actually delivered, count medication flushes and any other intake once, and compare the total with an individualized target. Prescribe additional water as needed rather than inferring a fixed amount from calorie density alone.

addedBodies.heading: Separate duration from destination
addedBodies.body: Nasogastric tubes are primarily used for short-term support. A longer anticipated course calls for reassessment of access, but duration and tube destination are separate questions: a gastrostomy reaches the stomach, while a jejunostomy reaches the small intestine. Longer support does not by itself mean that the tube must end in the jejunum. Check whether the stomach is usable, identify the actual tube tip, and assess the patient before choosing the access procedure. Tube feeding can supplement other intake or provide complete nutrition support.

addedBodies.heading: Account for each water source once
addedBodies.body: In a hypothetical water-budget exercise, 1,200 mL of formula labeled 80% water provides 960 mL of water. Add 300 mL of scheduled water flushes, 40 mL of separate medication water, and 100 mL of oral water: 1,400 mL total. Against a stated 1,500 mL daily target, 100 mL remains. These amounts are separate contributions, so do not count a medication flush again as a scheduled flush or add the entire formula volume a second time. Use what was actually delivered. The stated label and target are exercise inputs; this arithmetic does not establish a patient-specific water requirement or a safe flush schedule.

addedBodies.heading: Reassess hydration signals in context
addedBodies.body: Inadequate fluid intake during tube feeding can contribute to hypernatremia. Rising blood urea nitrogen (BUN) and reduced urine output also warrant assessment: dehydration can raise BUN, but impaired kidney function can do so as well. Review formula water content, delivered feeding volume, flushes, medication fluids, other intake, losses, and renal status instead of diagnosing the cause from formula density or BUN alone. Tailor the correction to the patient; adding fluid without assessing the total intake and the risk of fluid accumulation can be inappropriate.

workedWaterBudget.inputs: Hypothetical label fraction and target; no clinical target or water schedule established.

wholeObject.question: A patient receiving dantrolene has life-threatening hyperkalemia. Which distinction is correct?
choices: All forms of calcium are prohibited
Verapamil is the preferred calcium replacement
Calcium-channel blockers and calcium salts are interchangeable
Avoid calcium-channel blockers; IV calcium salts may still be indicated for hyperkalemia
wholeObject.rationale: The dantrolene interaction concerns calcium-channel blockers, which may cause marked hyperkalemia and cardiovascular collapse. MHAUS still includes IV calcium salts for life-threatening hyperkalemia. Therefore, all calcium is not prohibited. Verapamil is a calcium-channel blocker rather than calcium replacement, and calcium-channel blockers are not interchangeable with calcium chloride or gluconate.

individualChoices.text: All forms of calcium are prohibited
individualChoices.review: Incorrect: the calcium-channel-blocker interaction does not prohibit all calcium salts.

individualChoices.text: Verapamil is the preferred calcium replacement
individualChoices.review: Incorrect: verapamil is a calcium-channel blocker, not calcium replacement.

individualChoices.text: Calcium-channel blockers and calcium salts are interchangeable
individualChoices.review: Incorrect: calcium salts and calcium-channel blockers are different drug categories.

individualChoices.text: Avoid calcium-channel blockers; IV calcium salts may still be indicated for hyperkalemia
individualChoices.review: Correct: avoid calcium-channel blockers with dantrolene; indicated IV calcium salts remain in the MHAUS hyperkalemia pathway.

periop-mh-recognition.question: During sevoflurane anesthesia, end-tidal carbon dioxide rises despite ventilation and generalized rigidity appears before marked fever. Which response is best?
choices: Wait for a temperature above 42 C
Stop triggers, call for help, give oxygen and initiate dantrolene treatment
Give succinylcholine to treat the rigidity
Treat only the heart rate
periop-mh-recognition.rationale: Hypercapnia and generalized rigidity after sevoflurane warrant immediate MH treatment even before marked fever: stop triggers, call for help, provide oxygen and give dantrolene. Waiting for 42 C delays treatment. Succinylcholine is a trigger and adds danger rather than treating MH rigidity. Treating only heart rate leaves the triggering exposure and hypermetabolic process unaddressed.

periop-mh-volume.question: A 100-kg adult is prescribed an initial MHAUS dantrolene dose of 2.5 mg/kg using RYANODEX 250 mg reconstituted with 5 mL sterile water. What volume supplies that dose?
choices: 60 mL
2 mL
5 mL
30 mL
periop-mh-volume.rationale: The prescribed MHAUS dose is 2.5 mg/kg × 100 kg = 250 mg. A RYANODEX vial reconstituted with 5 mL supplies 50 mg/mL, so the dose occupies 5 mL. Two mL supplies only 100 mg; 30 mL would contain 1,500 mg at this concentration. The 60-mL reconstitution volume belongs to different 20-mg dantrolene products, not this 250-mg formulation. The prompt specifies a guideline-based dose; it does not redefine the product label.

periop-mh-label.question: A persistent MH crisis may require more than 10 mg/kg dantrolene under MHAUS guidance. How should this be described relative to RYANODEX labeling?
choices: It exceeds the listed label maximum and requires expert-directed crisis management and diagnostic reassessment
The label has no cumulative maximum
It is mandatory for every MH patient
It proves the diagnosis without reassessment
periop-mh-label.rationale: RYANODEX labeling lists a 10 mg/kg cumulative maximum. MHAUS recognizes that persistent contractures or rigidity can require more and advises alternative-diagnosis review if large doses fail to resolve symptoms. This is expert-directed crisis care beyond the listed limit. The label does have a maximum; exceeding it is not mandatory for every patient, and treatment nonresponse does not prove MH without reassessment.

periop-mh-calcium.question: A patient receiving dantrolene has life-threatening hyperkalemia. Which distinction is correct?
choices: All forms of calcium are prohibited
Verapamil is the preferred calcium replacement
Calcium-channel blockers and calcium salts are interchangeable
Avoid calcium-channel blockers; IV calcium salts may still be indicated for hyperkalemia
periop-mh-calcium.rationale: The dantrolene interaction concerns calcium-channel blockers, which may cause marked hyperkalemia and cardiovascular collapse. MHAUS still includes IV calcium salts for life-threatening hyperkalemia. Therefore, all calcium is not prohibited. Verapamil is a calcium-channel blocker rather than calcium replacement, and calcium-channel blockers are not interchangeable with calcium chloride or gluconate.

periop-mh-maintenance.question: An MH patient improves after initial treatment. Which MHAUS maintenance plan is appropriate?
choices: Stop dantrolene after the first normal temperature
Give 1 mg/kg IV every 4 to 6 hours for at least 24 hours with continued reassessment
Give one oral dose and discharge immediately
Continue the acute 2.5 mg/kg bolus every minute for 24 hours
periop-mh-maintenance.rationale: MHAUS recommends maintenance dantrolene 1 mg/kg IV every 4 to 6 hours for at least 24 hours, with continued assessment for recurrence and longer treatment when indicated. One normal temperature does not establish metabolic stability or satisfy all stopping criteria. An oral dose and immediate discharge do not provide this monitored IV regimen. Repeating acute 2.5 mg/kg boluses every minute for a day is not the maintenance schedule.

periop-mh-stopping.question: After 24 hours, an MH patient is afebrile but still has rigidity, rising CK and ongoing myoglobinuria. What follows?
choices: Temperature alone permits stopping therapy
ICU transfer automatically ends monitoring
Do not apply the MHAUS stopping criteria yet; continue specialist reassessment and treatment
Rising CK proves dantrolene allergy
periop-mh-stopping.rationale: MHAUS stopping or spacing criteria include 24 hours of metabolic stability, temperature below 38 C, decreasing CK, no ongoing myoglobinuria and resolved rigidity. This patient does not meet them. Normal temperature alone is insufficient, and transfer does not end monitoring. Rising CK indicates muscle injury in this context rather than proving dantrolene allergy; continue specialist reassessment and treatment.

periop-etomidate-infusion.question: Etomidate was selected for induction because blood pressure was marginal. A prolonged infusion is proposed for ongoing ICU sedation. What is the best response?
choices: Continue it because induction tolerability establishes infusion safety
Choose a different ongoing sedation plan because prolonged etomidate infusion risks sustained adrenal suppression
Continue it if a neuromuscular blocker prevents movement
Use it as both the sedative and sole analgesic
periop-etomidate-infusion.rationale: The etomidate label warns against prolonged infusion because it can prolong suppression of cortisol and aldosterone. Choose an appropriate ongoing sedation plan. Induction tolerability does not establish prolonged-infusion safety. A neuromuscular blocker conceals movement without removing endocrine risk or supplying sedation. Etomidate also lacks analgesic activity and cannot be the sole pain treatment.

periop-etomidate-analgesia.question: After etomidate induction, a painful procedure is planned. Which statement correctly addresses analgesia?
choices: Loss of consciousness establishes complete analgesia
Myoclonus proves analgesia is adequate
Etomidate has no analgesic activity, so pain treatment needs a separate plan
Adding paralysis supplies the missing analgesia
periop-etomidate-analgesia.rationale: Etomidate produces hypnosis without analgesic activity, so a painful procedure needs separate pain treatment. Loss of consciousness is not evidence of complete analgesia. Myoclonus is a recognized adverse effect and does not demonstrate pain control. Neuromuscular blockade suppresses movement without supplying analgesia.

periop-etomidate-dose.question: A 70 kg adult has an individualized order for etomidate 0.3 mg/kg IV. The vial contains 2 mg/mL. Which preparation and administration matches that order and the labeled usual injection duration?
choices: 10.5 mL over 30 to 60 seconds
21 mL over 30 to 60 seconds
1.05 mL over 30 to 60 seconds
10.5 mL as a prolonged maintenance infusion
periop-etomidate-dose.rationale: The ordered dose is 70 kg × 0.3 mg/kg = 21 mg; 21 mg ÷ 2 mg/mL = 10.5 mL. The usual labeled induction injection takes 30 to 60 seconds. A 21-mL preparation doubles the ordered dose; 1.05 mL gives only 2.1 mg, one-tenth of the order. A prolonged maintenance infusion is not this induction administration and is specifically discouraged because of adrenal suppression.

periop-etomidate-airway.question: An older patient receives etomidate and develops apnea. Which interpretation should guide the immediate response?
choices: Relative cardiovascular stability excludes an anesthetic complication
Wait for endocrine testing before providing ventilation
Treat movement suppression as evidence of adequate ventilation
Support the airway and ventilation immediately; etomidate can cause apnea
periop-etomidate-airway.rationale: Support airway and ventilation immediately. Apnea and partial upper-airway obstruction are reported with etomidate, even when cardiovascular effects are relatively limited. Cardiovascular stability does not exclude a respiratory complication. Waiting for endocrine tests delays immediate rescue, and absent movement does not establish adequate ventilation.

periop-ketamine-dilution.question: A prescribed 100 mg ketamine IV induction dose will be prepared from a 100 mg/mL vial. Which preparation follows the cited product label?
choices: Administer 1 mL undiluted IV
Dilute 1 mL with 1 mL of a labeled diluent, giving 2 mL at 50 mg/mL
Dilute 1 mL with 1 mL and administer only 1 mL for the full dose
Treat 100 mg/mL as the total vial content
periop-ketamine-dilution.rationale: One mL of 100 mg/mL contains the ordered 100 mg. Adding an equal 1-mL volume of a labeled diluent gives 2 mL at 50 mg/mL; use immediately after dilution. This product does not permit undiluted 100 mg/mL for IV induction. Giving only 1 mL after dilution supplies 50 mg rather than 100 mg. A concentration in mg/mL is not the total content of an unspecified vial.

periop-ketamine-procedure.question: Ketamine alone is proposed for a procedure involving mechanical stimulation of the pharynx because airway reflexes are retained. What is the best correction?
choices: Retained reflexes exclude laryngospasm
Retained reflexes eliminate aspiration risk
Ketamine alone reliably supplies the required muscle relaxation
Retained reflexes do not establish a safe sole-anesthetic plan for this procedure
periop-ketamine-procedure.rationale: Retained pharyngeal and laryngeal reflexes do not establish a safe sole-anesthetic plan for pharyngeal stimulation. The label advises against ketamine alone for pharyngeal, laryngeal or bronchial procedures. Laryngospasm and airway obstruction can occur; vomiting and aspiration remain possible. Ketamine does not reliably supply the required skeletal muscle relaxation, so the complete airway and anesthesia plan must be individualized.

periop-ketamine-interaction.question: A patient receiving aminophylline is being assessed for ketamine anesthesia. Which interaction is specifically relevant?
choices: Lower seizure threshold, prompting consideration of an alternative anesthetic
Complete blockade of ketamine analgesia
Guaranteed prevention of emergence reactions
Selective reversal of ketamine respiratory depression
periop-ketamine-interaction.rationale: The ketamine label identifies a lower seizure threshold with aminophylline or theophylline and advises considering an alternative anesthetic. It does not identify complete loss of ketamine analgesia, guaranteed prevention of emergence reactions or selective reversal of respiratory depression as the relevant interaction. Assess the medicines and anesthesia plan rather than assuming one drug protects against another adverse effect.

periop-ketamine-recurrent.question: A patient receiving recurrent ketamine develops severe urinary symptoms with suspected obstruction. What response matches current labeling?
choices: Continue unchanged because urinary toxicity occurs only after overdose
Treat the symptoms as routine emergence delirium
Discontinue ketamine and obtain urgent urological evaluation
Increase the dose to cover pain while postponing assessment
periop-ketamine-recurrent.rationale: Current ketamine labeling directs discontinuation and urgent urological evaluation for signs of obstruction or severe lower urinary tract symptoms. Serious urinary complications are reported with long-term use and are not restricted to acute overdose. These symptoms are not routine emergence delirium, and increasing the dose while deferring assessment continues exposure instead of addressing the complication.

periop-propofol-reserve.question: A frail, hypovolemic older adult needs induction. Which approach best addresses propofol risk?
choices: Use the usual healthy-adult dose rapidly because recovery is fast
Use cautious individualized titration with immediate airway and circulatory support
Increase the dose to compensate for older age
Treat absence of movement as proof of adequate ventilation
periop-propofol-reserve.rationale: Use cautious individualized titration with immediate airway and circulatory support. Propofol can cause profound hypotension and apnea; older, debilitated and unstable patients may need lower doses and slower administration. Rapid healthy-adult dosing does not become safe because recovery can be fast. Increasing the dose for older age opposes the label guidance, and absence of movement does not demonstrate ventilation.

periop-propofol-asepsis.question: A propofol vial was opened for an anesthetic procedure that has now ended after two hours. Under the cited label, what should happen to the remainder?
choices: Save it for another patient until twelve hours elapse
Refrigerate it for the next operating list
Add disinfectant to extend its use
Discard it and the dedicated administration materials as directed
periop-propofol-asepsis.rationale: For the cited Hospira product, discard unused propofol and dedicated administration materials at the end of the anesthetic procedure or 12 hours, whichever comes first. The two-hour procedure-end rule already applies. Saving it for another patient violates single-patient handling. Refrigeration does not extend this use period, and adding disinfectant is not an authorized preparation or preservation method.

periop-propofol-syndrome.question: During a propofol infusion, new unexplained metabolic acidosis, rhabdomyolysis and cardiac dysfunction develop. What is the best immediate medication response?
choices: Stop propofol, provide alternative sedation and urgently evaluate and treat the deterioration
Increase propofol to reduce metabolic demand
Wait until forty-eight hours of exposure before considering toxicity
Treat normal triglycerides as sufficient to exclude propofol toxicity
periop-propofol-syndrome.rationale: Stop propofol, provide alternative sedation and urgently evaluate and treat this pattern concerning for propofol infusion syndrome. Increasing the infusion continues a possible cause of the deterioration. The label also reports the syndrome after large-dose short-term surgical infusions, so do not wait for 48 hours. A normal triglyceride result does not exclude a syndrome characterized by metabolic and organ abnormalities, and is not a reason to delay assessment.

periop-propofol-calories.question: A nutrition review finds that propofol ran at 20 mL/hour for 24 hours. Using 1.1 kcal/mL, how much energy did it provide?
choices: 48 kcal
480 kcal
528 kcal
5,280 kcal
periop-propofol-calories.rationale: 20 mL/hour × 24 hours = 480 mL; 480 mL × 1.1 kcal/mL = 528 kcal. The 480 answer stops at volume and omits the energy conversion. The 48 answer is tenfold below the infused volume before applying the factor, and 5,280 is tenfold above the correct energy. Include the 528 kcal in the full nutrition review rather than treating propofol as nutritionally negligible.

periop-ketamine-neurologic-monitoring.question: Which statement accurately represents ketamine labeling for a patient with elevated intracranial pressure?
choices: No neurologic monitoring is needed because airway reflexes persist
The warning itself prohibits every use regardless of context
Use requires a monitored setting with frequent neurologic assessments and an individualized anesthesia plan

wholeFinalLesson.title: Make Posaconazole Formulation Visible
wholeFinalLesson.summary: Delayed-release tablets, oral suspension, and PowderMix differ in indication, eligibility, dosing, preparation, and exposure.
wholeFinalLesson.application: Select the formulation before the dose, then protect administration, exposure, interactions, and electrolyte surveillance.

lesson.heading: Stop unsafe substitution
lesson.body: Conventional posaconazole oral suspension is not substitutable with delayed-release tablets or PowderMix. A product switch requires a new indication, eligibility, dose, administration, and monitoring verification rather than a copied milligram amount. The February 2026 NOXAFIL label specifies delayed-release tablets for invasive aspergillosis treatment or high-risk prophylaxis in patients aged at least two years who weigh more than 40 kg. PowderMix covers those indications in children aged at least two years weighing 10 to 40 kg. Conventional oral suspension covers high-risk prophylaxis and oropharyngeal candidiasis in patients aged at least 13 years. Follow the exact product and indication rather than transferring one eligibility rule to every formulation. PowderMix is contraindicated in known or suspected hereditary fructose intolerance and requires its kit-specific preparation and provided notched-tip syringes.

lesson.heading: Use the current tablet instruction
lesson.body: Delayed-release tablets are swallowed whole and may be taken with or without food. This differs from older generalized teaching that every posaconazole dose must accompany a meal. Do not divide, crush, or chew the tablets. For eligible patients who cannot eat a full meal, the label favors tablets over conventional suspension for prophylaxis because tablets generally provide higher exposure. Food flexibility does not guarantee absorption: monitor for breakthrough infection with severe diarrhea or vomiting. The tablet food study still found an exposure change with a high-fat meal.

lesson.heading: Protect suspension absorption
lesson.body: Oral suspension is given with a full meal or, when needed, a nutritional supplement or acidic carbonated beverage. Give each conventional suspension dose during or within 20 minutes after a full meal. If a full meal is not possible and tablets or injection are not options, use the labeled liquid nutritional supplement or acidic carbonated beverage, such as ginger ale. If these cannot be tolerated either, consider an alternative antifungal or closely monitored suspension therapy. Shake well and use the provided measured dosing spoon. Assess poor intake, acid suppression, nausea, mucositis, diarrhea, and tube feeding before relying on oral delivery. Cimetidine and esomeprazole can lower suspension exposure; severe diarrhea or vomiting requires breakthrough monitoring. A healthy-volunteer NG-tube study found lower suspension exposure, but does not define every tube or continuous-feed protocol. Mucositis and nausea prompt intake assessment rather than a claimed uniform pharmacokinetic effect. PowderMix has separate with-food instructions and kit-specific preparation.

lesson.heading: Recognize mineralocorticoid excess
lesson.body: Hypertension, hypokalemia, and metabolic alkalosis can signal posaconazole-associated pseudoaldosteronism. Blood pressure, potassium, bicarbonate, exposure, renin, aldosterone, and competing causes guide evaluation. The current NOXAFIL label reports new or worsening hypertension, hypokalemia, low renin and aldosterone, and elevated 11-deoxycortisol in the postmarket setting. The FDA clinical review completed in May 2021 also describes metabolic alkalosis and reports associated with supratherapeutic posaconazole exposure during long-term use. Monitor blood pressure and potassium, characterize the acid-base pattern, and review the exact product, dose, interacting medicines and other possible causes. Hormone results and an interpretable drug concentration may help contextualize a suspected case; this is not a required fixed panel or a universal concentration cutoff. Pre-existing hypertension and concomitant steroids can complicate attribution. The pattern warrants evaluation rather than proving causation in every patient. Label-listed management options include discontinuing NOXAFIL, using an appropriate alternative antifungal not associated with pseudoaldosteronism, or an aldosterone-receptor antagonist; correct electrolyte disturbances as needed. Do not wait for every specialized result before monitoring or correcting the clinical abnormalities.

keyPoints: Current delayed-release tablets can be taken with or without food.
Suspension exposure depends on administration conditions.
Hypertension plus hypokalemia is a drug-safety signal.

all18FinalQuestionObjects.question: Which principle best characterizes posaconazole non-substitutability?
choices: Posaconazole delayed-release tablets, oral suspension, and PowderMix differ in indication, dosing, age or weight eligibility, preparation, and exposure
Every oral posaconazole product uses the same dose and preparation instructions
PowderMix is the conventional oral suspension in a different package
Age and weight can be ignored once the ingredient is identified
all18FinalQuestionObjects.rationale: The NOXAFIL label separates these oral products by indication, age and weight, dosing, preparation and exposure. Conventional oral suspension cannot replace delayed-release tablets or PowderMix dose for dose. A shared ingredient does not establish the same product, eligibility or administration plan.

all18FinalQuestionObjects.question: Which clinical action best applies to posaconazole non-substitutability?
choices: Select the formulation before selecting the dose
Select an oral dose first and assume it applies to both suspension and tablets
Choose the formulation after copying the previous milligram dose
Treat identical ingredient names as proof of identical oral exposure
all18FinalQuestionObjects.rationale: Identify the exact formulation before selecting its indication-specific dose and administration plan. The conventional oral suspension is not substitutable with delayed-release tablets or PowderMix. Selecting or copying a dose first, or treating the ingredient name as proof of equal exposure, bypasses those product requirements.

all18FinalQuestionObjects.question: Which assessment is most appropriate for posaconazole non-substitutability?
choices: Assess indication, age, weight, swallowing, food, tube access, formulation, and label
Use age alone because weight never affects posaconazole formulation eligibility
Treat all oral products as suitable for a feeding tube at the same milligram dose
Check the ingredient and dose but omit food and whole-tablet swallowing
all18FinalQuestionObjects.rationale: Check the indication, age and weight against the exact product label, then assess its food instructions and whether the patient can use that dosage form. Delayed-release tablets must remain whole, and conventional suspension has product-specific nutrition requirements. Tube access is a delivery assessment, not permission to crush tablets or assume equal tube exposure; the label's suspension NG-tube study found lower exposure and recommends breakthrough monitoring.

all18FinalQuestionObjects.question: Which reasoning hazard is most important to prevent with posaconazole non-substitutability?
choices: Substituting oral suspension for delayed-release tablets at the same dose
Reviewing the new formulation and its dosing regimen before a switch
Checking the suspension meal or nutritional-supplement plan
Confirming the dispensed formulation matches the intended order
all18FinalQuestionObjects.rationale: Conventional oral suspension is not substitutable with delayed-release tablets at the same milligram dose. Reviewing the new product and regimen, checking its nutrition plan, and confirming the dispensed formulation are appropriate checks. An ingredient match does not justify copying the dose or administration instructions.

all18FinalQuestionObjects.question: Which principle best characterizes posaconazole tablet administration?
choices: Delayed-release tablets are swallowed whole and can be taken with or without food
Delayed-release tablets must always be taken with a full meal
Crushing a delayed-release tablet preserves its labeled administration technique
The conventional suspension food rule applies to every posaconazole product
all18FinalQuestionObjects.rationale: NOXAFIL delayed-release tablets may be taken with or without food and must be swallowed whole without dividing, crushing or chewing. Requiring a full meal for every tablet dose copies the conventional suspension rule to the wrong product. Food can change tablet exposure in the label's healthy-volunteer study; permission to dose without food does not mean food has no pharmacokinetic effect.

all18FinalQuestionObjects.question: Which clinical action best applies to posaconazole tablet administration?
choices: Use the tablet when eligible and reliable higher oral exposure is needed
Keep conventional suspension fasting because tablets and suspension always produce equal exposure
Choose delayed-release tablets without checking indication, age, weight or swallowing
Crush the tablet whenever the patient cannot swallow it whole
all18FinalQuestionObjects.rationale: For an eligible patient who cannot eat a full meal, the label favors delayed-release tablets over conventional suspension for prophylaxis because tablets generally provide higher plasma exposure. Eligibility and intact swallowing still matter, and severe diarrhea or vomiting warrants breakthrough monitoring. This is product selection to improve delivery, not guaranteed exposure or better clinical outcomes; equal exposure, unchecked eligibility and crushing are unsafe assumptions.

all18FinalQuestionObjects.question: Which assessment is most appropriate for posaconazole tablet administration?
choices: Assess ability to swallow whole, gastrointestinal function, weight, indication, adherence, and interactions
Confirm the indication but assume swallowing and gastrointestinal symptoms cannot affect delivery
Check daily milligrams and ignore the product's age and weight eligibility
Assume tablets remove the need for adherence and medication-interaction review
all18FinalQuestionObjects.rationale: Assess intact swallowing, gastrointestinal symptoms, labeled eligibility, actual adherence and interacting medicines before relying on the tablet plan. The label permits food flexibility, but prohibits tablet manipulation and calls for breakthrough monitoring with severe diarrhea or vomiting. Eligibility, adherence and CYP3A4 interaction review are not waived by changing from suspension to tablets.

all18FinalQuestionObjects.question: Which reasoning hazard is most important to prevent with posaconazole tablet administration?
choices: Repeating the older rule that every posaconazole tablet dose requires food
Teaching that the delayed-release tablet may be taken with or without food
Confirming the tablet is swallowed whole without dividing, crushing or chewing
Checking the exact product before giving meal instructions
all18FinalQuestionObjects.rationale: The current NOXAFIL delayed-release tablet instruction permits administration with or without food. Repeating a universal food requirement confuses it with conventional oral suspension. Teaching the current tablet instruction, preserving whole-tablet administration and checking the formulation are appropriate actions. Give the patient the instructions for the exact dispensed formulation.

all18FinalQuestionObjects.question: Which principle best characterizes posaconazole suspension administration?
choices: Oral suspension is given with a full meal or, when needed, a nutritional supplement or acidic carbonated beverage
Conventional oral suspension is routinely taken fasting like the delayed-release tablet
Any clear drink makes fasting suspension exposure equivalent to a full meal
Adding an acidic beverage removes the need to review interacting drugs or breakthrough risk
all18FinalQuestionObjects.rationale: Give conventional NOXAFIL oral suspension during or within 20 minutes after a full meal. When a full meal cannot be eaten and tablets or injection are not options, the label permits a liquid nutritional supplement or an acidic carbonated beverage such as ginger ale. Routine fasting, an arbitrary clear drink, or using a beverage to bypass interaction and breakthrough review does not follow that plan. PowderMix is a separate delayed-release product with its own with-food and preparation instructions.

all18FinalQuestionObjects.question: Which clinical action best applies to posaconazole suspension administration?
choices: Protect absorption and monitor for breakthrough when adequate intake cannot be achieved
Continue the suspension fasting and assume the prescribed dose ensures absorption
Assume a proton pump inhibitor cannot affect suspension exposure
Treat identical tablet and suspension milligrams as identical absorbed doses
all18FinalQuestionObjects.rationale: Protect the conventional suspension nutrition and delivery plan, and monitor for breakthrough when adequate intake cannot be achieved. If a full meal is impossible, review the labeled alternative formulation or supplement/acidic-beverage options; if those cannot be tolerated, consider another antifungal or closely monitored suspension therapy. Fasting with assumed absorption, ignoring an esomeprazole interaction, or equating tablet and suspension milligrams does not establish adequate exposure.

all18FinalQuestionObjects.question: Which assessment is most appropriate for posaconazole suspension administration?
choices: Assess meal, supplement, acid suppression, nausea, mucositis, diarrhea, tube feeds, and alternative formulation
Review meal timing alone and ignore vomiting, diarrhea and interacting drugs
Treat any acid-suppressing medicine as having the same proven effect on every posaconazole formulation
Assume tube feeds make conventional suspension and crushed tablets interchangeable
all18FinalQuestionObjects.rationale: Assess the actual nutrition plan, interacting medicines and delivery route, including nausea or mucositis that may make the prescribed intake difficult. The label identifies lower suspension exposure with cimetidine or esomeprazole and lower exposure in a specific NG-tube study; severe diarrhea or vomiting requires breakthrough monitoring. These findings do not establish one effect for all acid suppressants, all tube/feed arrangements or mucositis, and they do not authorize crushing delayed-release tablets.

all18FinalQuestionObjects.question: Which reasoning hazard is most important to prevent with posaconazole suspension administration?
choices: Giving suspension fasting without an exposure plan
Confirming the suspension is taken with a full meal
Planning an oral nutritional supplement when needed for suspension administration
Reviewing acid-suppressing medicines and the exact formulation
all18FinalQuestionObjects.rationale: Giving conventional suspension fasting without a nutrition and exposure plan bypasses its labeled administration requirements. A full meal is the first choice; when it is not possible, review the product-specific supplement/acidic-beverage fallback and alternative formulations. Checking the meal plan and relevant interacting medicines are appropriate actions, not additional hazards.

all18FinalQuestionObjects.question: Which principle best characterizes posaconazole pseudoaldosteronism?
choices: Posaconazole can cause hypertension and hypokalemia through apparent mineralocorticoid excess
Pseudoaldosteronism requires elevated aldosterone and cannot occur with suppressed renin and aldosterone
Posaconazole-related mineralocorticoid excess raises potassium rather than lowering it
New hypertension during posaconazole excludes a drug-related cause if the patient already had hypertension
all18FinalQuestionObjects.rationale: The current NOXAFIL warning identifies new or worsening hypertension with hypokalemia and reports low renin and aldosterone with elevated 11-deoxycortisol. Thus high aldosterone is not required, potassium may fall, and prior hypertension does not exclude worsening from a drug-associated syndrome. Postmarketing reports do not establish its frequency or prove causation in every patient.

all18FinalQuestionObjects.question: Which clinical action best applies to posaconazole pseudoaldosteronism?
choices: Recognize the pattern, review exposure, and manage the drug and electrolyte consequences
Replace potassium alone and ignore the new blood-pressure pattern and posaconazole exposure
Increase posaconazole whenever hypokalemia develops because the pattern proves underexposure
Wait for every specialized hormone result before monitoring blood pressure or correcting potassium
all18FinalQuestionObjects.rationale: Recognize the paired blood-pressure and potassium change, review the exact product, dose, exposure and competing causes, and manage the clinical consequences. The label calls for blood-pressure and potassium monitoring; options include discontinuation, an appropriate alternative antifungal, or an aldosterone-receptor antagonist. The FDA 2021 review links reported cases with supratherapeutic exposure, not proven underexposure. Potassium replacement alone does not resolve the whole assessment, and immediate monitoring and correction need not await a universal hormone panel. No concentration cutoff or fixed treatment sequence is established here.

all18FinalQuestionObjects.question: Which assessment is most appropriate for posaconazole pseudoaldosteronism?
choices: Assess blood pressure, potassium, bicarbonate, renin, aldosterone, posaconazole concentration, and interacting causes
Measure blood pressure only because potassium and the acid-base pattern are unrelated to this syndrome
Interpret one drug concentration as definitive proof and omit competing medicines or causes
Require elevated renin and aldosterone before considering posaconazole-associated pseudoaldosteronism
all18FinalQuestionObjects.rationale: Assess blood pressure and potassium first, then use bicarbonate to characterize possible metabolic alkalosis and interpret renin, aldosterone, drug exposure and competing causes in clinical context. The current label reports low renin and aldosterone with elevated 11-deoxycortisol; the FDA 2021 review describes alkalosis and reports associated with supratherapeutic posaconazole levels. Blood pressure alone misses the electrolyte pattern. One concentration cannot prove causation, and high renin or aldosterone is not required. This is a contextual assessment, not a mandatory fixed testing panel or a universal drug-level threshold.

all18FinalQuestionObjects.question: Which reasoning hazard is most important to prevent with posaconazole pseudoaldosteronism?
choices: Attributing the entire pattern to essential hypertension
Checking the potassium and bicarbonate pattern alongside new or worsening hypertension
Reviewing posaconazole exposure and competing causes before assigning causation
Interpreting renin and aldosterone in context rather than requiring them to be elevated
all18FinalQuestionObjects.rationale: Essential hypertension alone should not explain away new or worsening hypertension paired with hypokalemia and possible metabolic alkalosis during posaconazole use. Reviewing electrolytes, exposure, hormones and competing causes helps evaluate the drug-safety signal; these are appropriate actions, not the hazard. Prior hypertension or concomitant steroids can complicate attribution, and temporal association alone does not establish causation.

Dispensing unchanged or assuming equal exposure is unsupported, and crushing the delayed-release tablet is explicitly prohibited.

wholeObject.question: During parenteral treatment for suspected Wernicke encephalopathy, a patient has documented hypomagnesemia and incomplete early neurological improvement. Which action is most appropriate?

individualChoices.text: Declare thiamine ineffective and stop it without reviewing magnesium or competing causes.
individualChoices.review: Incorrect: incomplete early improvement is not a reason to stop thiamine without reviewing magnesium and other causes.

individualChoices.text: Give unrestricted magnesium to every patient regardless of the value or kidney function.
individualChoices.review: Incorrect: unrestricted magnesium ignores measured levels, kidney function and monitoring.

individualChoices.text: Wait until a fixed thiamine course ends before assessing the documented magnesium deficiency.
individualChoices.review: Incorrect: a fixed thiamine-course end is not a reason to postpone assessment of documented low magnesium.

False: no unreviewed stopping because response incomplete.
False: renal and level-dependent dosing required.
False: documented deficit needs timely review, not arbitrary end-course delay.
priorReviewFields.singleBestAnswerReview: Magnesium supports conversion of thiamine to its active form, and hypomagnesemia can impair response. Recheck and correct the documented deficiency while continuing appropriate thiamine treatment and reviewing other causes. Replacement must account for kidney function, severity and monitoring; neither unrestricted magnesium nor delaying assessment until a fixed course ends is appropriate.
